sources.title: Can Black Holes or Other Relativistic Space Objects Be a Source of Dark Energy?

evidence.text: Compare the redshift trend quoted from a referenced black-hole/stellar-mass analysis with the direction implied by growth with scale factor. For gravastars, sum matter and compact-object density-pressure contributions and discuss whether negative pressure could dominate.

sources.title: Black holes as the source of dark energy: A stringent test with high-redshift JWST AGNs

evidence.text: The applied correction is BBH=Bs,vir+BL⋆+Bm,vir(Hα), with adopted components −0.3, −0.5 and −0.3 dex. The authors include these negative shifts as a conservative test. They omit positive biases, stating that including those would lower inferred k.

sources.title: Can Black Holes or Other Relativistic Space Objects Be a Source of Dark Energy?

evidence.text: Use conservation-based mass accounting for accretion, collapse and mergers, then compare the assumed mass scaling with comoving-volume scaling and the cosmological acceleration criterion involving ρ+3P.

sources.title: Black holes as the source of dark energy: A stringent test with high-redshift JWST AGNs

evidence.text: The local fit has central relation log10 MBH=8.66+1.32 log10(M⋆/10^11 M⊙). Combining it with cosmological growth gives μi(k)=1.32 log10 M⋆,i−k log10(1+zi)−5.86. A product Gaussian likelihood compares μi with bias-corrected logarithmic BH masses; BH mass error, converted stellar-mass error and intrinsic scatter are added in quadrature.

sources.title: Black holes as the source of dark energy: A stringent test with high-redshift JWST AGNs

evidence.text: Selection requires z>4, broad-Hα significance >5σ, E(B−V)<0.1, images without unresolved point sources or disks, and SFR below an adopted redshift-dependent main-sequence criterion. The adopted main-sequence scatter is 0.1 dex for 0<z≤6 and 0.4 dex for 6<z≤10.

sources.title: Observational Evidence for Cosmological Coupling of Black Holes and its Implications for an Astrophysical Source of Dark Energy

evidence.text: Can reported preferential SMBH growth relative to host stellar mass be explained by cosmological mass coupling, and could a population of similarly coupled stellar-remnant black holes supply dark energy?

sources.title: Can gravitational vacuum condensate stars be a dark energy source?

evidence.text: Can the internal pressure of stable compact objects, particularly gravastars, source cosmological dark energy, and what motion follows if their proper masses are directly coupled to cosmic expansion?

sources.title: Comment on “Observational Evidence for Cosmological Coupling of Black Holes and its Implications for an Astrophysical Source of Dark Energy”

evidence.text: Does restricting the Einstein–Hilbert variation to a homogeneous scale factor justify the spatially averaged cosmological equation used to connect black-hole mass growth with dark energy, when matter sources are already inhomogeneous at leading order?
